Hi Sam / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap + suggested next steps from our side so we keep momentum:

Summary of needs you confirmed on the call:
- SDK + auth: server-side SDK integration (Node/Python) with SSO-backed auth for admin actions; prefer OIDC or SAML for enterprise SSO.
- Routing: region-aware routing (US primary, EU for EU traffic) and a cost/latency policy to route low-latency requests to a premium instance and bulk async jobs to a cheaper quantized model.
- Structured output & tool-calling: model must support structured JSON outputs and safe tool-calling for internal enrichment calls.
- Embeddings & reranker: we’ll index product docs with 1536-d embeddings and use a lightweight reranker for top-k precision.

Immediate asks / next steps I propose:
1) Tech contacts: please share the SSO admin and infra lead emails so we can scope auth flow (ideally before EOD Mon).
2) PoC scope: we’ll propose a 3-week PoC: SDK onboarding (week 1), embeddings + reranker (week 2), routing + fallback (week 3). I attached an MVP-integration-checklist.
3) Architecture diagram: Dev will sketch a recommended topology (regions, routing, cache layers) and share a PNG.
4) Contracting touchpoint: Ellen in procurement? If yes, cc her when we convert to a SOW.

Notes on model-routing / policy knobs (high level):
- Latency policy: requests tagged as interactive => route to low-latency pool (higher cost); background/batch => route to quantized cost-optimized pool.
- Fallback chains: primary model -> smaller local quantized variant -> remote hosted fallback (different model family) with request scoring to detect divergence.
- Region routing: client IP or tenant metadata drives region selection; optional geofencing for compliance.

Attaching the checklist and will follow up with an architecture sketch by EOD Monday. If you want to jump on a 30-min technical sync, we can do Tue/Wed next week — share availability.

Hey Sam — short technical follow-up from my side.

Auth / SDK:
- We recommend server-side SDKs for any request that uses customer secrets. Client SDKs can be used for anonymous or masked flows.
- For SSO: OIDC flow + short-lived service tokens for SDK servers; we also support IdP-initiated SAML if your SSO team prefers.

Embeddings / reranker:
- Typical flow: chunk docs -> embed (1536) -> vector DB (we test with Pinecone/Weaviate) -> initial retrieval -> reranker call to model (structured score + highlight spans).
- Reranker should be a smaller cross-encoder; we can serve it on Dedicated capacity to avoid cold starts.

Model routing & fallback specifics:
- Policy primitives we can configure via the Console API: tag (interactive, batch), max-latency-ms, cost-priority (low|medium|high), allowed-model-families.
- Example policy rule: if (tag==interactive && max-latency-ms<=150) => route to ml-llamax-70B-lowlatency; else if (batch) => ml-opt-6.7b-quant.
- Fallback chain is implemented as a list; each hop can enable response-quality-check functions (nucleus sampling entropy, length mismatch) which triggers the next hop.

Structured outputs / tool calling:
- We provide a schema-driven generation helper; you can register tool-call endpoints that models can invoke (e.g., fetch_customer_profile). Calls return structured JSON which the runtime validates against the declared schema.

I sketched a simple topology and attached it (redwood-orbitlytics-arch.png). Happy to walk through this on a tech call.

—Dev

Hi Sam / Elena —

Answers inline and next steps below.

On Mon, Feb 22, 2026 at 09:12 AM Samuel Lin <sam@orbitlytics.com> wrote:
> 1) Regional routing: can we pin specific tenants to EU-only models and ensure no token or prompt material leaves EU region?

Yes — we support tenant-level routing policies. For EU-only tenants we deploy model replicas in EU region and enforce egress rules so requests and cache KV remain in-region. We can present a short tech note for your compliance team.

> 2) Fallback behavior: if primary model triggers fallback to hosted remote model, are logs/payloads redacted/observed differently? We need to ensure PII never goes to third-party hosted models.

By default, fallbacks to hosted remote models can be enabled or disabled per-tenant. If enabled, we can apply a data-sanitization hook pre-fallback (regex PII scrub + structured field filters). For strict compliance we recommend disabling remote fallbacks and instead using an on-prem or dedicated quantized variant as the second hop.

> 3) Cost reporting: will we get token-level cost/breakdown per route so we can model run-rate?

Yes — Console provides token-level breakdowns by route/model with daily export. We can also push a streaming usage feed into your billing pipeline for near-real-time reporting.
